Historical trends built into the projections

TrendWhat the history says
Age curveBox-score production peaks around 27–28. The average player's BPM change is about zero at 24 and about −0.36 per year by 29. Athletic stats fade first.
Years 2–4 leapMost Improved Player winners average year 4 in the league, and leaps cluster at ages 24–25. Second-to-third-year jumps are a documented pattern (FiveThirtyEight's "junior jump").
Veteran declinePlayers 36 and older who aren't stars lose production faster than the general age curve shows. Stars who still score 22+ points a game, like Stephen Curry and Kevin Durant, tend to hold their level longer.
Contract yearThe effect is small. One study found a 2.83% PER gain, but only after excluding superstars. Another found a 3–5 percentile boost for the median player, and some studies find no effect. So the bump is modest and skips stars.
Injury returnFirst seasons back from these injuries usually come with lower efficiency and managed minutes.
Games playedProjections start from each player's recent games played, then I adjust for known injuries and age. A player who misses a third of the season leaves your roster spot empty for weeks, and a per-game rank hides that cost.
